The New, Redesigned Avalon Tiny Home Ditches Loft Living for a Spacious Single-Level Layout
26 photos
Photo: Dragon Tiny Homes
Loft bedrooms are a great design solution for small spaces, as they help maximize the use of space through vertical living and thus increase available square footage. But lofts are not for everyone, because climbing up and down ladders or steep storage stairs to reach the bed can be difficult or painful for some groups of people, like seniors or children.
For many people who have embraced the tiny house lifestyle, there is nothing more luxurious than having a ground-floor bedroom. Apart from eliminating the need to climb ladders or stairs at bedtime, it offers plenty of other benefits, like increased comfort, privacy, full standing height, and easy to move around.
Recognizing these advantages, more and more tiny house builders are integrating single-level layouts into their lineups. One of them is Dragon Tiny Homes, which has just revealed a new iteration of its Avalon 32 model with a single-level configuration and a cozy downstairs bedroom.
The Avalon is the largest model in Georgia-based Dragon Tiny Homes’ lineup, and this new version makes good use of its 32-foot (9.7-meter) length to offer single individuals or couples a commodious, functional living space. While previous versions of the Avalon tiny house tried to maximize vertical space by adding lofts to create extra sleeping or storage space, this new unit keeps everything on one floor, prioritizing everyday comfort rather than squeezing as much function as possible into a compact footprint.
Photo: Dragon Tiny Homes Built on a triple-axle trailer, the home measures 8.5 feet (2.6 meters) wide and approximately 13.5 feet (4.1 meters) tall, and it still packs a lot of living space into a package that remains towable. With a weight of 18,000 lbs, the builder says a Ford F-350 or a similar truck could be used to tow it.
The home’s exterior is clad in engineered wood siding, with owners able to pick the color palette. This latest unit completed by Dragon Tiny Homes is finished in a combination of lime green and gray, which gives it a lively, contemporary appearance. White window trim and a matching front door frame pull the colors together, creating a cohesive look.
The interior offers a 269-square-foot (25-square-meter) footprint with full-height ceilings throughout. Many compact homes featuring single-floor layouts are all about open-space living . They usually have no separation between the lounging and sleeping areas, or even have flexible bedroom arrangements that double as lounging spaces during the day. This is not the case with Avalon, as this home is large enough to offer separation between common and private rooms.
Photo: Dragon Tiny Homes The open-plan living room and kitchen occupy the center of the house, while the bedroom is at the rear of the trailer and the bathroom at the front. This arrangement allows the private rooms to remain separate from the main living space, which is an important perk for owners planning to live in the home full-time .
The central area is flooded with natural light from multiple large windows strategically placed along both side walls, capturing daylight from different angles. The luminosity and airiness of the space is enhanced by the white walls and matching white-paneled ceiling with high-reflectivity finish.
The living room is fitted with a sofa on a built-in platform that cleverly incorporates storage cubbies underneath. A wall-mounted television and an electric fireplace constitute the entertainment setup, while a wooden shelf above the sofa provides space for displaying plants, books, and photos.
A side table and another wall-attached drop-down table are also included, the latter providing a practical spot for dining or working. A massive picture window frames the outside view, turning this area into your private “observation room.”
Photo: Dragon Tiny Homes The kitchen is equally luminous and airy and provides a well-equipped space for cooking everyday meals. It features all-white cabinetry with contrasting black hardware and is equipped with a sink, an induction cooktop, a microwave, and an apartment-sized refrigerator.
Near the kitchen, a wooden barn-style sliding door opens into the bathroom, which is cleverly compartmentalized to differentiate between its functions. A narrow delineates the toilet area from the laundry space and another one separates the shower from the linen closet. The vanity, sink, and mirror are located in the front bump-out, a signature feature on Dragon Tiny Homes designs.
Photo: Dragon Tiny Homes At the opposite end of the house, the bedroom offers all the perks we mentioned above. It is spacious enough to fit a full-size bed with a memory foam mattress and built-in storage, a wardrobe cabinet, and shelving, and because it sits on the main floor, dwellers can stand upright and move around comfortably. The separation from the living room also provides a level of privacy that it’s hard to achieve in a home with a bed that doubles as a sofa during the day.
Certified by the National Organization of Alternative Housing (NOAH), which means it meets the highest standards for safety, quality, and compliance with building codes, this new Avalon 32 tiny house is listed for sale, asking for US$73,850.
